page.overview:
What is Dreamlands?

The Dreamlands (also known as the Dream Realm) are a fictional setting created by H. P. Lovecraft for a series of stories, known as the Dream Cycle, set in a world that people enter through their dreams. It is a vast, alternate dimension or universe, with lands, seas, creatures, civilisations, and an extensive Underworld.

The Dreamlands are for the most part a mirror-image of our waking universe, having, as far as can be determined, the same planets, stars, and other cosmic geographical features. However, there are numerous races, civilisations, and beings existing in the Dreamlands that do not exist in the waking universe, such as the Zoogs, Gugs, Ghasts, moon-beasts, and others.

In keeping with the dimension's nature as the consensus of Earth's dreams, it is easier to travel to distant places including other planets or the Moon than it would be in the physical waking world. The journey may still be long or have requirements to be met but travel to distant "locations" in the Dreamlands is relatively commonplace.

Also, the Dreamlands usually refers to the Dreamlands of Earth; however the overarching Dream realm includes a "Dreamlands" for every world inhabited by intelligent life. For example if Mars still had intelligent life, as some writers suggest, it too would have a Dream realm of its own and those falling asleep and dreaming on Mars would enter the same Dreamlands but in a vastly distant and presumably different set of entry points to those of Earth's Dreamers.

connections.short_description: Xura is a coastal region in the Dreamlands of Earth, also known as the "Land of Pleasures Unattained", which first appeared in H. P. Lovecraft's short story "The White Ship".
